Yes, visceral adipose tissue (VAT) area measurement at a single level, specifically 3 cm above the lower margin of the L3 vertebra, can represent changes in VAT volume and body weight. This method has been shown to be feasible and can reflect interval changes in VAT volume and body weight. However, it's essential to note that VAT area measurement should be selected at this location due to advances in knowledge suggesting that VAT area at a CT slice 3 cm above the lower margin of L3 is more accurate for reflecting interval changes.

Additionally, it's crucial to consider other factors that can influence VAT volume, such as body weight and overall health status. A comprehensive approach involving multiple measurements and assessments may provide a more accurate understanding of VAT volume and its relationship with body weight.

It's also worth mentioning that VAT area measurement at different locations on the abdomen may yield varying results, highlighting the need for further research to establish standardized guidelines for VAT assessment.
